main_text.p: confugiunt ad potentes viros, vt si per infci-tiam non possunt, vincant per personam.

2 Sed quid respondet Christus? Negat Moses mandasse: sed permisisse tantum, idque ob singularem duritiem cordis eorum, vitandi nempe maioris mali causa, ne forte interficerent uxores, vt Hieronymus exponit, aut in coniugio scortarentur: sed Deum creatorem a principio non sic ordinasse, cuius ordinatio perpetuo valere debeat. Moses, inquit, πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν (quam Moses ipse, Israeli non semel exprobrauit, nominatim vero Deuter. 9. & 31.) permisit (non praecepit, quasi Deo probaretur, aut natura rectum esset: neque enim is probat diuortium, qui hoc maluit admitti, quam homicidium) vobis repudiare uxores vestras: caeterum ab initio non fuit sic: quum scilicet nondum increuisset hominum malitia: neque nunc relaxabitur idem ius, postea quam euangelica doctrina renouat ac perficit naturae synceritatem. Sequitur enim in responsione Christi, Dico autem vobis, quod quicunque repudiauerit uxorem suam, nisi ob stuprum (mulier enim scortando se quasi putridum membrum a viro resecindens, eum liberat, vñ bricht die ehe,) & aliam duxerit, is committit adulterium. Et qui repudiatam duxerit, is adulterium committit. Quanquam haec verba (quibus Christus indicat, quatenus liceat dimittere, aut non) Marcus cap. 10. seorsum discipulis suis fuisse dicta refert, quum domum venissent.

page.notes: Greek phrase "πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν" is printed in Greek; the first word is hard to make out at the scan resolution and is marked as printed-looking, not verified. The German words in black letter ("vñ bricht die ehe") are uncertain and may read differently. The word "infci-tiam" at the line break is uncertain. The page number "190" at top left is uncertain. Long s has been written as plain s throughout; the printed "Mofes", "Christi", "sic" etc. are read as Moses, Christi, sic. The catchword "sent." is the start of the next page's word split across the line break.
